headline: Quiet Monday: Qwen4-Max hit the HN front page
summary: Nothing big today, just one new model and two small updates.

items.title: Qwen4-Max is out, HN is talking about it
items.pitch: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max made it to the top of HN with lots of comments. Take a quick look, but don't rush to switch tools.
why: 596 points and 250 comments on HN, the hottest AI thing today
Qwen is one of the open-source model families overseas developers use a lot
All we've seen so far is the title and the buzz, so the actual abilities aren't verified yet
actions: Open the official page and see if there's a way to chat with it and try it right away
deep_dive: Unlike the Claude and codex you use now, Qwen is a model from a different company. You don't need to change anything in your daily work for now.
The source only has the title and the buzz, with no pricing, benchmarks, or info on how it's offered. Don't make up your mind before you try it.

items.title: Codex may have fixed the "at capacity" error
items.pitch: Someone on the Codex team says that annoying "model at capacity" error might be fixed. If you use codex, give it another try.
why: That error can interrupt your work
The poster is Thibault Sottiaux, a Codex team member

items.title: A skill that gets better the more you use it
items.pitch: Dan Shipper says they built a skill that "gets better every time you use it." He used it to write context summaries and got it to about 80% of what he likes.
why: People who use skills may not have to keep tweaking them by hand
He used autoresearch (letting the AI try things over and over and fix itself) to iterate
For now it's just one tweet, with nothing you can install yet
